findings.reason: folding the instruction into the existing block is a smaller, contract-consistent change than a parallel read obligation, and the plan's §4/§7 text would say so.
findings.text: §4 adds a checkpoint read obligation beside the existing `PEER CHANNEL` block, which is already the contract's single run-directory read and already instructs the worker to list/read its durable channel; the design gives no reason the existing block cannot carry a coordinator-authored instruction. The honest change is to extend that block, so the worker keeps one read discipline rather than two that can drift.

findings.reason: naming the owner converts §4/§7 from "build an inbox and a writer" into "extend the peer channel for a non-run author", which is the plan's whole remaining half and changes its deliverable and its contention analysis.
findings.text: the plan's §4 inbox ("a coordinator writes a message into the run's own directory") and §7's "coordinator-side writer" re-create, for the coordinator→worker direction, the durable message store the peer channel already owns at `_channel_root`/`peer_ask`/`peer_list` (`run_dir/<run>/peer-channel/questions/*.json`); the plan never names that owner, so an implementer will fork a second run-directory message store. The real gap — a coordinator has no run id, so `peer_ask` cannot yet be its author — is exactly the justification the plan must state, and extending the owner (a coordinator-authored message kind plus the §4 checkpoint read) is the change that gap calls for.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the one new module the plan lands, `reckon/hooks/worker_message_guard.py`, hides the scope test, host-local identity resolution and refusal composition behind a single `decide(payload) -> (allowed, message)`; §4's other half edits an existing contract and a CLI path rather than adding modules, so no surface is spread thin.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the coordinator-side writer and the inbox store duplicate the per-run peer-channel owner in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` (`_channel_root`, `peer_ask`, `peer_list`, endpoint `run_dir/<run>/peer-channel`) instead of extending it, and the plan names no owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched: §3 reuses the native-agent guard's interception point (`reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py`) and the `reckon sync` hook-install wiring rather than inventing an interception, and its §4 research comment names the existing peer-channel block as the one run-directory read the contract already performs.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 obliges the worker to read its run directory at checkpoints, but the prompt contract already carries exactly one run-directory read (the `PEER CHANNEL` block, `reckon/crew/prompts.py:619`) and the plan does not say why that block cannot be extended to carry the instruction.
